To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cells in spontaneous and chemically-induced mouse hemangiosarcromas and hemangioma are of endothelial cell origin.
mouse hemangio-sarcomas and -angiomas are composed primarily of cells derived from CD34 ^{+}, CD31 ^{+}, and VEGFR2 ^{+} EPCs that have not yet fully differentiated.
mouse hemangiosisarcomas and hamangiomas are composed mainly of cells derived from endothelial progenitor/stem cells expressing CD34 and VEGFR2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of hemangioma and hemangiosar-coma in mice.
the identification and characterization of mouse hemangiosacromas and hemangioma cells and their relationship to EPCs.
the identification of the cell of origin of spontaneous and cheminally induced hemangiosarcomas and hemangiomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hemangiosarco-mas and hemangioma are composed of cells that are of EPC origin, and that these cells express EC markers but not hematopoietic cell markers.
mouse hemangioendothelial cell tumors are composed of ECs that express EC markers but not hematopoietic markers, indicating that they arise from EPC-derived cells.
the cells of origin of mouse vascular tumors are EPCs that express CD34, Vegfr2, and CD 31 but not factor VII-related antigen and are not derived from myeloid lineage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the process of spontaneous or chemical-induced hemangiosar-coma formation in mice involves recruitment of bone marrow–derived EPCs that show some degree of EC differentiation.
mouse hemangio- sarcomas and hemagiomas are composed of endothelial cells that are at a later stage of differentiation than the endothelial progenitor stage.
mouse hemangioendotheliomas and hemangiomas arise from EPC-derived cells that are at an early stage of differentiation and do not express factor VIII–related protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the origin of hemangiomas and hemangiosaromas in mice is from EPCs, which are arrested in their development and do not express mature EC markers such as factor VIII–related antigens.
mouse hemangio sarcomas and hemangio mas may arise from ECPs that are at the stage of CD34, V EGFR2, and C D31 but not factor V III–related antigen expression.
mouse hemangiasarcomas and hamangiomas are composed primarily of EPCs expressing the endothelial differentiation markers CD34, VEFGR2, and CD 31 but not factor-VIII related antigen.
